Title: February 2026 Inflation Update
#### March 2026 Inflation. # February 2026 Inflation Update. With all the news coming out of the Middle East, we’ve updated our Inflation-Adjusted Oil Price History Chart and Historical Oil Prices Tables. We’ve updated the Historical Steampunk calculator that calculates annual inflation all the way back to 1774, and it is just plain fun to use. Check out our Current Inflation page or Annual Inflation. Annual Average Inflation Chart since 1774. ## Now, back to the Inflation News. ## The BLS reported Annual Inflation at 2.4%, unchanged from last month. ## Annual Inflation Table. |  | Jan | Feb | Mar | Apr | May | Jun | Jul | Aug | Sep | Oct | Nov | Dec |. *“The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.3 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in February, after rising 0.2 percent in January, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. *The all items index rose 2.4 percent for the 12 months ending February, the same increase as reported for the 12 months ending January.”*. This month, unemployment is up 0.1% and inflation is also up slightly, so the misery index is up to 6.81%.

# Inflation Update. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) released the report on the September Consumer Price Index (CPI). But what did it learn about inflation? The key series – year-over-year topline inflation and year-over-year core inflation – are shown below. Both the CPI and the core CPI registered inflation of 3.0 percent. Inflation is on the rise, having hit its recent low in April 2025. It has been three years since inflation peaked in 2022. With inflation at 2 percent, a dollar is only worth 94 cents in another three years. Inflation at 3 percent, it means that same dollar is worth only 91 cents. There is a reason to get inflation back to the 2 percent target. In response to the report, Bloomberg reported: “While still illustrating that inflation remains well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target, the softer-than-expected CPI report sealed expectations for the Fed to cut interest rates at next week’s policy meeting, and boosted the odds of a further move in December.” With each cut in rates, the Fed signals that it is willing to accommodate inflation that is above its target, perhaps substantially so, for a sustained period. Abandoning a return to the 2 percent target would be a mistake comparable to letting inflation get out of hand in 2021. Douglas Holtz-Eakin is the President of the American Action Forum. Douglas Holtz-Eakin is the President of the American Action Forum. ### Consumer Price Index. Measures the change in prices of all goods and services purchased for consumption by urban households. ### Core Consumer Price Index. Consumer Price Index excluding food and energy. ### Core Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index. A measure of prices paid for goods and services excluding food and energy; the Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation. ### Producer Price Index. Measures the change in selling prices received by domestic producers of goods and services. ### ISM Services Index. The core questions cover three broad areas of consumer sentiment: personal finances, business conditions, and buying conditions. Measures change in private-sector employment using ADP payroll data covering more than half a million companies with more than 25 million employees.
